description.value: The study investigated MAPT H1 and H2 haplotypes in relation to frontotemporal dementia and functional alterations of cerebral glucose metabolism using FDG PET imaging.

spans.text: The aim of this study was to investigate whether the extended MAPT haplotypes H1 and H2 are associated with FTD and to explore whether inheritance of these haplotypes translates functionally to different patterns of cerebral glucose metabolism.

description.value: Patients with frontotemporal dementia and cognitively healthy comparison subjects were studied in a population-based comparison and a PET substudy.

spans.text: The authors investigated MAPT haplotypes in 142 individuals with FTD and 292 comparison subjects.

value: Two extensive clusters with reduced glucose utilization in the left frontal cortex were detected in the H2 group as compared with the H1 group after controlling for age at onset, duration, gender, and cognitive test scores. These areas included the superior and medial frontal gyri in both hemispheres and the left inferior frontal gyrus. No differences in metabolism patterns were observed for the reverse comparison, that is, when H1 metabolism was less than H2 metabolism.
